## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- vercel:auth: Authentication integration guidance — Clerk (native Vercel Marketplace), Descope, and Auth0 setup for Next.js applications. Covers middleware auth patterns, sign-in/sign-up flows, and Marketplace provisioning. Use when implementing user authentication.
- vercel:bootstrap: Project bootstrapping orchestrator for repos that depend on Vercel-linked resources (databases, auth, and managed integrations). Use when setting up or repairing a repository so linking, environment provisioning, env pulls, and first-run db/dev commands happen in the correct safe order.
- vercel:chat-sdk: Vercel Chat SDK expert guidance. Use when building multi-platform chat bots — Slack, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, GitHub, Linear — with a single codebase. Covers the Chat class, adapters, threads, messages, cards, modals, streaming, state management, and webhook setup.
- vercel:deployments-cicd: Vercel deployment and CI/CD expert guidance. Use when deploying, promoting, rolling back, inspecting deployments, building with --prebuilt, or configuring CI workflow files for Vercel.
- vercel:env-vars: Vercel environment variable expert guidance. Use when working with .env files, vercel env commands, OIDC tokens, or managing environment-specific configuration.
- vercel:knowledge-update: Corrects outdated LLM knowledge about the Vercel platform and introduces new products. Injected at session start.
- vercel:marketplace: Vercel Marketplace expert guidance — discovering, installing, and managing integrations via the `vercel integration` CLI, with auto-provisioned environment variables and unified billing. Use when consuming third-party services on Vercel.
- vercel:microfrontends: Guide for building, configuring, and deploying microfrontends on Vercel. Use this skill when the user mentions microfrontends, multi-zones, splitting an app across teams, independent deployments, cross-app routing, incremental migration, composing multiple frontends under one domain, microfrontends.json, @vercel/microfrontends, the microfrontends local proxy, or path-based routing between Vercel projects. Also use when the user asks about shared layouts across projects, navigation between microfrontends, fallback environments, asset prefixes, or feature flag controlled routing.
- vercel:next-cache-components: Next.js 16 Cache Components guidance — PPR, use cache directive, cacheLife, cacheTag, updateTag, and migration from unstable_cache. Use when implementing partial prerendering, caching strategies, or migrating from older Next.js cache patterns.
- vercel:next-forge: next-forge expert guidance — production-grade Turborepo monorepo SaaS starter by Vercel. Use when working in a next-forge project, scaffolding with `npx next-forge init`, or editing @repo/* workspace packages.
- vercel:next-upgrade: Upgrade Next.js to the latest version following official migration guides and codemods. Use when upgrading Next.js versions, running codemods, or migrating between major releases.
- vercel:nextjs: Next.js App Router expert guidance. Use when building, debugging, or architecting Next.js applications — routing, Server Components, Server Actions, Cache Components, layouts, middleware/proxy, data fetching, rendering strategies, and deployment on Vercel.
- vercel:react-best-practices: React best-practices reviewer for TSX files. Triggers after editing multiple TSX components to run a condensed quality checklist covering component structure, hooks usage, accessibility, performance, and TypeScript patterns.
- vercel:routing-middleware: Vercel Routing Middleware guidance — request interception before cache, rewrites, redirects, personalization. Works with any framework. Supports Edge, Node.js, and Bun runtimes. Use when intercepting requests at the platform level.
- vercel:runtime-cache: Vercel Runtime Cache API guidance — ephemeral per-region key-value cache with tag-based invalidation. Shared across Functions, Routing Middleware, and Builds. Use when implementing caching strategies beyond framework-level caching.
- vercel:shadcn: shadcn/ui expert guidance — CLI, component installation, composition patterns, custom registries, theming, Tailwind CSS integration, and high-quality interface design. Use when initializing shadcn, adding components, composing product UI, building custom registries, configuring themes, or troubleshooting component issues.
- vercel:turbopack: Turbopack expert guidance. Use when configuring the Next.js bundler, optimizing HMR, debugging build issues, or understanding the Turbopack vs Webpack differences.
- vercel:vercel-agent: Vercel Agent guidance — AI-powered code review, incident investigation, and SDK installation. Automates PR analysis and anomaly debugging. Use when configuring or understanding Vercel's AI development tools.
- vercel:vercel-cli: Vercel CLI expert guidance. Use when deploying, managing environment variables, linking projects, viewing logs, querying metrics, managing domains, or interacting with the Vercel platform from the command line.
- vercel:vercel-connect: Vercel Connect expert guidance — securely obtain scoped OAuth tokens for third-party services (Slack, GitHub, MCP servers, OAuth, Snowflake) on behalf of apps or users via Vercel OIDC. Use when wiring up third-party API access, connecting to MCP servers, sending Slack messages, accessing GitHub APIs, receiving webhook events from Slack/Linear/GitHub and forwarding them to your agents and apps, or building Eve agent connections.
- vercel:vercel-firewall: Vercel Firewall expert guidance — automatic DDoS mitigation, the Vercel WAF (custom rules, IP blocking, managed rulesets, rate limiting), Attack Mode, system bypass, bot management, and the `vercel firewall` CLI. Use when configuring platform-level security, responding to attacks, or staging firewall rules.
- vercel:vercel-functions: Vercel Functions expert guidance — Serverless Functions, Edge Functions, Fluid Compute, streaming, Cron Jobs, and runtime configuration. Use when configuring, debugging, or optimizing server-side code running on Vercel.
- vercel:vercel-sandbox: Vercel Sandbox guidance — ephemeral Firecracker microVMs for running untrusted code safely. Supports AI agents, code generation, and experimentation. Use when executing user-generated or AI-generated code in isolation.
- vercel:vercel-storage: Vercel storage expert guidance — Blob, Edge Config, and Marketplace storage (Neon Postgres, Upstash Redis). Use when choosing, configuring, or using data storage with Vercel applications.
- vercel:verification: Full-story verification — infers what the user is building, then verifies the complete flow end-to-end: browser → API → data → response. Triggers on dev server start and 'why isn't this working' signals.
- vercel:workflow: Vercel Workflow DevKit (WDK) expert guidance. Use when building durable workflows, long-running tasks, API routes or agents that need pause/resume, retries, step-based execution, or crash-safe orchestration with Vercel Workflow.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use when: morning brief, daily brief, set up my morning brief, what's my day look like, run my brief.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
55	        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
56	        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
57	        │
58	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
59	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
60	        │
61	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
62	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
63	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
64	```
65	
66	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
67	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
68	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
69	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
70	
71	## 4. Authentication and credentials
72	
73	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
76	| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
77	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
78	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
79	
80	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
81	
82	## 5. Data exchanged
83	
84	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
87	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
88	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
89	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
90	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
91	
92	No PII flows through Contentful.
93	
94	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
95	
96	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
97	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
98	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
99	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
100	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
101	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
102	
103	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
104	
105	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
106	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
107	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
108	
109	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
110	
111	| Failure | Behaviour |
112	|---|---|
113	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
114	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
115	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
116	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
117	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
118	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
119	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
120	
121	## 9. Security and privacy
122	
123	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
124	- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
125	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
126	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
127	
128	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
129	
130	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
131	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
132	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
133

        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001). It manages editorial content,
banners, size guides, promotional content, and global assets. Integration is via the Contentful Delivery
API (CDA) for all customer-facing pages, with the Contentful Preview API (CPA) available server-side only.

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.
Environment IDs match SFCC tier names exactly — no mapping required at runtime.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | DEV | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 3 | TEST | `test` | `npm run push:test` | zimmermann-test.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com (to be created) |

| 5 | STAGE | `staging` | `npm run push:staging` | zimmermann-stg.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 6 | UAT | `uat` | `npm run push:uat` | zimmermann-uat.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 7 | PRODUCTION | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Per tier | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Per env, server-side only | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

Locale Configuration
--------------------

Nine locales matching SFCC `config/sites.js` exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| `en-US` | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| `en-GB` | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |
| `fr` | French | ZimmermannEUfr | en |
| `it` | Italian | ZimmermannEUit | en |
| `es` | Spanish | ZimmermannEUes | en |
| `en-CH` | English (EU International) | ZimmermannEUIntl | en |
| `en-HK` | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| `en-AE` | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

Content Type Management
-----------------------

|  | Editorial content types | Studio Experiences definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |
| **Deploy** | `npm run sync:contentful` or migration | Imported at runtime — no push step |
| **Current types** | shoppableImage | CollectionHero, ImageText, ShoppableImage |

### Migration format

export const id = '002-my-change';

// Use the contentful-management plain client

* **Contentful roles:** Assign a “Content Editor” role on `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, and `master` that can CRUD entries/assets but cannot edit content types. Only the CI service account can modify content types in those environments.

Standard Objective/Background/Tasks/DoD spike house style.

**Ticket timeline (comments):**
- 8 Jul — Jasmijn tags the group to connect on drafting the TSD.
- 21 Jul — Jhoan posts a first draft (`Contentful Integration TSD_SFCC123.docx`).

- 22 Jul (today) — **you** hand Jhoan a spike-specific TSD skeleton (`sfcc-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md`), "seeded from repo, Confluence, and related Jira stories."

⚠️ That skeleton is a **Jira attachment only** — it is **not** in the repo or scratchpad. (Contrast SFCC-122, whose deliverable lives at `zimmermann-pwa/.docs/spikes/SFCC-122-mrt-api-capabilities.md`.)

# TSD: Contentful Integration — SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)

> **Status:** 🟡 In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** {{YYYY-MM-DD}}
> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) + Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.

<!-- SCOPE GUARD: a TSD addresses one problem/solution, not "all the other stuff". This one is
     legitimately broad because its single job is "brief the incoming Contentful squad on the SFCC-side
     integration". Keep every section lean and LINK the sources above — do not reproduce them. -->

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** {{one sentence — e.g. "Give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful↔SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC needs, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope."}}

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale config, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Link, don't specify.

<!-- The ticket's Objective/Background go here in 2-3 lines, then link the Jira ticket. -->

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

<!-- Pull the pattern + diagram from .docs/integration/02-contentful.md §3-§5 and the ops page's "Architecture".
     State it once, at briefing altitude. Confirm each surface still matches the code in §3. -->

**Pattern [seed — verify against 02-contentful.md §3]:** Contentful → MRT (Node/SSR) → browser, SSR-first for SEO/LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content — SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts — MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net — srcset/sizes, AVIF→WebP
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages — one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface           | Origin / boundary | Token                                           | Notes                                                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| CDA (published)   | Browser + SSR     | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first; browser hydrates from SSR payload            |
| CPA (drafts)      | MRT proxy only    | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side)        | Contentful Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI host only      | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`                   | Never in MRT/bundle — build-time only                   |
| Publish webhook   | Contentful → MRT  | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC)                     | Cache purge; TTL fallback 60s SWR                       |

<!-- Confirm: SSR cache TTL/SWR, GraphQL-vs-REST split, CDN rate limit (55 rps/token) — from 02-contentful.md §6. -->

      "value": "1-overview1. Overview
---------------------

Product data in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is managed through a **master catalogue** (`zimmermann-catalog`) with per-site **storefront catalogues** for navigation and category assignment. Product content (rich text, editorial imagery) is managed in **Contentful CMS**.

AP21 is the system of record for all product data. Product data flows from AP21 into SFCC via **MuleSoft** — there is no direct AP21 → SFCC integration. MuleSoft acts as the integration layer, transforming and routing product data into SFCC catalogue XML imports.

---

2-product-data-architecture2. Product Data Architecture
-------------------------------------------------------

DefaultnoneAP21 (ERP — system of record for products)
│
└──► MuleSoft (integration layer — transform + route)
│
└──► zimmermann-catalog (SFCC master catalogue)
│ products + variants + attributes
│
├──► zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog (AU nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-uk-storefront-catalog (UK nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-us-storefront-catalog (US domestic nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-us-intl-storefront-catalog (US International / Global-e nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-eu-storefront-catalog (EU nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-eu-intl-storefront-catalog (EU International / Global-e nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-hk-storefront-catalog (HK nav categories)
└──► zimmermann-me-storefront-catalog (ME nav categories)
Contentful CMS
│
└──► PWA Kit (editorial content: banners, editorial copy, lookbook)
via Contentful Delivery API

---

3-master-catalogue-structure3. Master Catalogue Structure
---------------------------------------------------------

**Catalogue ID:**`zimmermann-catalog`

### 31-category-hierarchy-all-storefront-catalogues3.1 Category Hierarchy (all storefront catalogues)

| Position | Category ID | Display Name | Sub-categories |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `new-arrivals` | New | — |
| 2 | `clothing` | Clothing | dresses, tops, bottoms, knitwear, jackets, swimwear |
| 3 | `accessories` | Accessories | bags, shoes, jewellery |
| 4 | `collections` | Collections | resort |
| 5 | `z-immerse` | Z.Immerse | — |
| 6 | `sale` | Sale | — |

**Magento-sourced category hierarchy** (used during Magento migration — see Section 11):

Defaultnoneroot
└── {prodline} (L1 — e.g. "collection")
└── {prodline}-{prodsub} (L2 — product assignment target, e.g. "collection-tops-blouse")

`categoryap21` is an internal AP21 ERP code — stored as a hidden custom attribute (`ap21Category`) on the product, not used for storefront navigation.

### 32-product-model3.2 Product Model

SFCC product types in use:

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Master product | Top-level product identified by `stylecode` — holds variation attributes (colour, size), images, descriptions |
| Variant product | Individual purchasable SKU — `stylecode` + `colourcode` + `sizecode` |
| Color group (Magento) | Style + colour SKU in Magento (`visibility = Catalog, Search`) — maps to master product body |

**Product ID conventions:**

| SFCC Role | ID Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Master | `stylecode` | `4673TS251` |
| Variant | `stylecode` + `colourcode` + `sizecode` | `4673TS251GVSCP0P` |

---

4-catalogue-import-process4. Catalogue Import Process
-----------------------------------------------------

### 41-initial-load-sample-data4.1 Initial Load (Sample Data)

A filtered sample catalogue (`data/sample/catalogs/zimmermann-catalog/`) is used for development and staging bootstrapping.

**Import command:**

Defaultbashnpm run data:import:sample

### 42-ongoing-product-feed4.2 Ongoing Product Feed

| Step | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Source | AP21 (ERP) — system of record for all product master data |
| Integration layer | MuleSoft — receives product events from AP21, transforms to SFCC Catalog XML, and delivers to SFCC |
| Format | SFCC Catalog XML (catalog.xsd compliant) |
| Target | `zimmermann-catalog` (master) + per-site storefront catalogues |
| Trigger | MuleSoft event-driven (AP21 product create / update) or scheduled batch — to be confirmed with MuleSoft team |
| Import method | MuleSoft → SFCC OCAPI Data API (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFCC SFTP + import job |

### 43-product-imagery4.3 Product Imagery

Product images are loaded directly into SFCC — there is no Cloudinary or external DAM involved. Images are stored in the SFCC static content library and referenced from product records by path.

| Aspect | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Storage | SFCC static content library (loaded directly) |
| Source | AP21 / DAM — images are uploaded directly to SFCC; no Cloudinary or external DAM in the pipeline |
| Image types | Large, medium, small/thumbnail, hi-res model shot, swatch/styling shot |
| Migration reference | Magento image paths used as source reference during initial load only |

---

5-storefront-catalogue-assignment5. Storefront Catalogue Assignment
-------------------------------------------------------------------

Each site's storefront catalogue is set in `preferences.xml` via `SiteCatalog`:

| Site | Storefront Catalogue |
| --- | --- |
| ZimmermannAU | `zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannUK | `zimmermann-uk-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannUS | `zimmermann-us-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannUSIntl | `zimmermann-us-intl-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannEU | `zimmermann-eu-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannEUIntl | `zimmermann-eu-intl-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannHK | `zimmermann-hk-storefront-catalog` |
| ZimmermannME | `zimmermann-me-storefront-catalog` |

The master catalogue assignment (linking storefront categories to master products) is managed in SFCC Business Manager — it cannot be set via XML import.

---

6-contentful-cms-integration6. Contentful CMS Integration
---------------------------------------------------------

| Aspect | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Editorial content: hero banners, collection pages, lookbook, rich PDP copy |
| Rendering | PWA Kit fetches content at runtime via Contentful Delivery API |
| Scope | Non-product content; all product data remains in SFCC catalogue sourced from AP21 via MuleSoft |

---

7-multilocale-product-content7. Multi-Locale Product Content
------------------------------------------------------------

| Site | Locales | Language Tags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ZimmermannAU | en | `x-default`, `en` |
| ZimmermannUK | en, en\_GB | `x-default`, `en`, `en-GB` |
| ZimmermannUS | en, en\_US | `x-default`, `en`, `en-US` |
| ZimmermannUSIntl | en, en\_US | `x-default`, `en`, `en-US` |
| ZimmermannEU | en, en\_GB, fr, it, es | `x-default`, `en`, `fr`, `it`, `es` |
| ZimmermannEUIntl | en, en\_CH | `x-default`, `en`, `en-CH` |
| ZimmermannHK | en, en\_HK | `x-default`, `en`, `en-HK` |
| ZimmermannME | en, en\_AE | `x-default`, `en`, `en-AE` |

Product XML attributes use `xml:lang` for each locale. The `x-default` value is always English.

---

8-product-display-page-pdp--mulesoft-touchpoints8. Product Display Page (PDP) — MuleSoft Touchpoints
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

MuleSoft is the integration layer for the product import pipeline (see Section 4.2). In addition, the PDP has two further MuleSoft-dependent runtime features:

| Feature | API | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find In Store / Boutique Stock | `product-availibility-prc-api` | Real-time store stock availability shown on PDP |
| Real-time DC stock check | [TBC] | Online availability from NewStore fulfilment groups |

---

9-key-design-decisions9. Key Design Decisions
---------------------------------------------

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product source of truth | AP21 | AP21 is the ERP and master for all product data |
| Product integration layer | MuleSoft | Consistent with Zimmermann integration platform; MuleSoft handles AP21 event consumption, transformation, and SFCC delivery |
| Product imagery | Loaded directly into SFCC | No external DAM or Cloudinary in the pipeline; images stored in SFCC static content library |
| Catalogue structure | One master + eight storefront catalogues | SFCC best practice for multi-site |
| Editorial content | Contentful | Decouples editorial from product data; supports headless PWA pattern |
| Category positions | Explicit `<position>` elements per category | Ensures nav order matches Figma design across all sites |
| USIntl separate storefront catalogue | `zimmermann-us-intl-storefront-catalog` | Allows independent category assignment for Global-e international customers |

*Last updated 2026-07-16. Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. Requirement IDs (e.g. DMU-030, REG-041) reference the **Zimmermann Functional Requirements** spreadsheet.*

---

1. Purpose & Scope
------------------

This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at <http://www.zimmermann.com> — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.

**In scope:**

* Stack and build pipeline
* The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
* Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 8 storefronts in 6 regions
* Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
* SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
* Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
* Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
* Open decisions requiring client input before build

**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design

---

2. Solution Overview
--------------------

A single PWA Kit codebase serves 8 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.

The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

Legend / boundaries:

* **PWA → Contentful, Vimeo, Didomi, GTM (via Addingwell), Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, Narvar Promise, Adyen Drop-In, Measmerize:** browser-direct; no SFCC involvement. GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, and Narvar Promise load post-Didomi-consent only.
* **PWA → Google Maps, GiveX balance check, MuleSoft (select direct calls), Booxi:** MRT-mediated — called from the Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/`; credentials held as MRT environment variables, never in the browser bundle.
* **PWA → SFCC:** all commerce data (catalogue, cart, pricing, customer, orders) via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`.
* **SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore / AP21 / Omneo / Narvar:** write and sync flows initiated by SFCC.
* **AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (inbound):** product and pricing master feed into the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks.
* **Omneo iFrame (My Account):** also surfaced as a browser-direct iFrame in My Account (CRM-176); all other Omneo traffic via MuleSoft.
* **PWA (MRT) → MuleSoft → NewStore:** read flows — order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check. SFCC is not in this path.
* **SFCC server-side integrations (cartridge-based unless noted):** Avalara, Adyen server API, GiveX (via NewStore adapter).
* **Global-e (two surfaces):** (1) browser handoff iframe at checkout for international orders (PAY-054); (2) server-side pricing/catalogue feed into SFCC (PRC-34..43).

---

3. Frontend Stack
-----------------

### 3.1 Bundled by PWA Kit

| Layer | Library | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base framework | PWA Kit on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 | Current baseline |
| UI framework | React 18 + Chakra UI | Component library + theme tokens |
| Routing | React Router v6 |  |
| Server / async state | TanStack Query via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` | All SFCC data fetching |
| i18n | react-intl | Translations under `translations/` |
| Build / dev | Webpack 5 via `pwa-kit-dev` |  |

### 3.2 Project additions

| Layer | Library | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type safety | TypeScript strict mode | All custom code is `.ts` / `.tsx` |
| Component explorer | Storybook 8 + `@storybook/addon-a11y` | `play` functions for interaction tests |
| Unit testing | Vitest (+ `vitest-axe`) | Project-level test runner |
| E2E | Playwright (+ `axe-playwright`) | Multi-region fixtures from day one |
| Forms | react-hook-form + zod | Introduced when checkout / account work begins |
| Global UI state | Zustand | Per-request store in SSR |

---

4. Customisation Model
----------------------

This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's *template extensibility* model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.

All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.

**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.

**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) will also live in the `overrides/` folder.

### 4.1 Environment Configuration

All secrets and per-tier identifiers are injected as **Managed Runtime environment variables**. Unless public identifiers, they must never be committed to source control or exposed in client-side bundles. The canonical list of every variable the storefront expects is maintained in the project's environment-variable template, grouped by integration with inline comments — that template is the single source of truth. The table below shows the groups so each credential's boundary is clear.

| Group | Purpose | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMMERCE_API_*`, `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` | SFCC SCAPI / SLAS client config | Browser-direct (public client ID) + MRT-mediated (token refresh) |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` | Google Maps Places API (address autocomplete) | MRT-mediated — key never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Contentful Delivery API (published content) | Browser + SSR. CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle but held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_HOST` | Contentful Preview API (drafts, editor sessions) | MRT-mediated — proxied server-side; never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Contentful Management API (schema sync) | **Local / CI only** — never deployed to MRT |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Shared secret for the Contentful → MRT cache-purge webhook (HMAC verification) | MRT-mediated |
| `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | PWA → MuleSoft direct calls (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`): order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock, GiveX balance | MRT-mediated — credentials never reach the browser |
| `ADYEN_CLIENT_KEY`, `ADYEN_ENVIRONMENT` | Adyen Drop-In / Components SDK at checkout (tokenisation, 3DS2 inline). Server-side `/payments` calls and HMAC live in SFCC BM | Browser-direct — client key is public by design (PAY-021) |
| `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` | Inside Chat support widget. **Likely NOT PWA-owned** — Inside Chat loads via GTM script injection through the Addingwell container (HPC-039/040), so its token sits inside the GTM container config (Tell No Lies), not a PWA env var. Retain only if the PWA must initialise the widget itself; confirm with Tell No Lies | Browser-direct — public token (if used at all) |
| `NARVAR_ACCOUNT_ID` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD widget at checkout (domestic only) | Browser-direct — public ID |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 site key (registration / login forms) | Browser-direct — public site key only |
| `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 secret key — used by the MRT layer to verify tokens against Google's `siteverify` endpoint; never reaches the browser | MRT-mediated |
| `GLOBALE_*` | Global-e merchant ID, environment, script host, supported countries, server-side API key | Browser-direct (script host, merchant ID) + MRT-mediated (API key, if used) — final shape pending PRC-34..43 sign-off |
| `DIDOMI_API_KEY` | Didomi Notice/Consent ID | Browser-direct — public ID, safe in bundle |
| `GTM_CONTAINER_ID`, `GTM_SERVER_URL` | GTM container and Addingwell first-party tagging-server hostname (`<https://ruffles.zimmermann.com`).> The loader uses both: `${GTM_SERVER_URL}/gtm.js?id=${GTM_CONTAINER_ID}` | Browser-direct — both public, safe in bundle. One pair per environment |
| `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY`, `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` | Observability | MRT-mediated (license keys held server-side); `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (one of `local`, `dev`, `sit`, `stage`, `uat`, `prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry / New Relic / GTM |
| `MARKETING_CLOUD_*`, `COMMERCE_AGENT_SETTINGS`, `OTP_TOKEN_LENGTH` | PWA Kit base-template defaults referenced by the base runtime configuration | Likely removable once email/auth wiring is finalised (Zimmermann uses Emarsys via Omneo, not Marketing Cloud) |

**Security policy:**

* Real values live only in local, untracked environment files — one shared file (`.env.shared`, tier-independent) plus one per deployment tier (`.env.<tier>` for dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`). Only a template — variable names tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on their own comment line, no secret values — is committed to source control as `.env.sample`. Two guardrails enforce this: a pre-commit hook that blocks commit if `.env.sample` contains a secret-shaped non-empty value, and a Claude Code rule that instructs the AI assistant never to write real secret values into `.env.sample`.
* Public identifiers (e.g. the GTM container ID, Didomi notice ID, SFCC SLAS client ID) may carry placeholder values in the committed template.
* Secrets (tokens, license keys, HMAC secrets, server-side API keys) appear in the committed template as the variable name only, with an empty value.
* Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
* MRT variables are managed per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase.

---

5. Multi-Site, Multi-Locale Architecture
----------------------------------------

### 5.1 Storefronts

**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions**, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods. 11 active locales total. US/EU domestic and international are configured as separate SFCC sites (REG-006).

| Locale | URL prefix | Currency | Checkout owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AU + Oceania | `/` (x-default hreflang) | AUD | SFCC (REG-003) |
| UK | `/uk/` | GBP | SFCC (REG-004) |
| US domestic | `/us/` | USD | SFCC (REG-005) |
| US international | `/en-ca/` | USD | Global-e (REG-005) |
| EU domestic — EN / FR / IT / ES | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR | SFCC (REG-006 dom) |
| EU international | `/en-ch/` | EUR | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK | `/hk/` | HKD (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-007) |
| ME | `/en-ae/` | AED (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-008) |

Rest-of-world traffic routes via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` (DMU-013). AU is configured at the root with no locale prefix and serves as the x-default hreflang target (DMU-016).

### 5.2 Entry routing

* **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
* **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
* **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.

### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale

Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.

### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed

* **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
* **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
* **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
* **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.

### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

* **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
* **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
* **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
* **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

---

6. Checkout Ownership Branching
-------------------------------

Checkout owner is determined at PDP / cart, not only at the checkout page — so price, shipping, duty, and tax presentation are correct before the customer commits.

* **SFCC owns:** AU domestic (including Oceania — Avalara for NZ + New Caledonia), UK, US (when shipping to US), EU domestic.
* **Global-e owns:** HK, ME, EU international, the US site when shipping outside the US, and any domestic storefront when the selected shipping destination is outside that storefront's market.
* **Pricing for Global-e markets (REG-041):** SFCC holds all pricebooks (including Global-e ones), derived nightly from AP21 base prices and Global-e FX/coefficients. SFCC sends the complete cart in target currency at handoff; Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from that point. Full mechanism specified under PRC-34..43.
* **Global-e shipping country lock (REG-028):** locked at the country selector pre-checkout; cannot change once inside Global-e.

---

7. Integration Map
------------------

### 7.1 Classification model

Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.

* **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
* **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
* **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
* **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
* **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).

A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.

> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

### 7.2 Integration map

| System | Role | Call origin | Hosting layer | Security |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **SFCC (SCAPI)** | Storefront, catalogue, basket, customer, orders, BM config, domestic checkout | Browser (Shopper API via `commerce-sdk-react`) + MRT (token refresh, OCAPI residue) | Browser-direct + MRT-mediated | SLAS client ID public in bundle; SLAS client secret on MRT for the public-client PKCE flow; refresh tokens set as `httpOnly` cookies by the Node layer, never visible to JS |
| **Contentful — Delivery (CDA)** | Published editorial content (on live website) | MRT + Browser | Browser-direct + MRT-mediated | CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle. SSR-first for SEO/LCP, browser hydration uses the SSR payload |
| **Contentful — Preview (CPA)** | Editor preview sessions, draft content | MRT (SSR pass and editor proxy) | MRT-mediated | CPA token is semi-sensitive (exposes drafts); held server-side and proxied through MRT — never reaches the browser |
| **Contentful — Management (CMA)** | Schema sync (`npm run sync:contentful`), Studio editor OAuth | Out-of-band (CI host) | Out-of-band | CMA token never embedded; stored as a CI environment variable on the host that runs the sync |
| **Contentful publish webhook** | Cache invalidation on entry publish | Contentful → MRT | MRT-mediated | Webhook receiver in the Node/SSR layer; shared-secret HMAC verification on the incoming request |
| **Vimeo** | Product video hosting — PDP gallery, runway / campaign clips (PRD-066/067) | Browser (lazy iframe embed) | Browser-direct | Embed URL stored in product data or the CMS; no secret. 8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation
-------------------------------

### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)

All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.

#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type

PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.

| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP states | **SSR shell + CSR data** | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven |

The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.

### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang

Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.

### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots

Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.

### 8.4 Structured data

Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:

* **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
* **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
* **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
* **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).

### 8.5 URL strategy

* Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
* Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
* 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.

### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)

No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

9. Performance Strategy
-----------------------

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule

Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.

### 9.2 Other levers

* **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
* **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:

  + **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  + Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
* Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
* Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured

The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.
